主要内容: PwC US released a 2012 tax rate benchmarking study for industrial products and services companies, revealing that the average three-year effective tax rate (ETR) for industrial product (IP) companies through December 31, 2011, was 26.3 percent, a 0.7 percent increase from the prior year's 25.6 percent. Many ETRs were lower than statutory rates due to foreign operations and tax incentives for research and innovation. U.S.-based companies had higher ETRs than their global counterparts, while Canadian and German companies reported lower ETRs. The study highlights the impact of economic recovery on ETR volatility, with increased corporate earnings reducing sectoral volatility. The report also emphasizes the importance of transfer pricing, especially for companies expanding into emerging markets, and the challenges posed by inconsistent intercompany transfer pricing laws and aggressive tax enforcement by authorities. The analysis covers six sectors: aerospace & defense, chemicals, engineering & construction, industrial manufacturing, metals, and transportation & logistics.
